_provenance.source_pdf: Nicolas Slonimsky - Thesaurus OfScales And Melodic Patterns.pdf

polation_operations._description: Three coined operations Slonimsky applies to principal tones of an equal-division progression. Each yields a different decorated shape, and they compose freely. Categorical primitives for the melodic engine's then-action vocabulary.

operations.definition: Insertion of one or more notes BETWEEN principal tones.
Insertion of a note BELOW a principal tone.
Insertion of a note ABOVE the next principal tone.
Compound: interpolation + ultrapolation in the same figure.
Compound: all three operations in the same figure.
Interpolation at equal intervals from pivotal points; produces palindromic interval structure.

equal_division_progressions._description: The structural backbone of the Thesaurus. Each progression divides one or more octaves into equal parts; principal tones of that division are then decorated via polation operations.

interval_taxonomy._description: Slonimsky's tone-distance vocabulary. The 'sesqui-' prefix uniformly adds a semitone. Coined names for intervals where common practice uses tonal-functional labels.

progression_taxonomy._description: Slonimsky's structural categories for distinguishing types of melodic lines. The Scale-vs-Pattern distinction is fundamental: it determines whether polation operations preserve or reverse direction.

categories.definition: A progression that changes direction only at terminal points. All interpolated progressions are Scales.
A melodic figure in which direction changes before terminal point. All infrapolated and ultrapolated progressions are Patterns.
Umbrella term for any scale or pattern.
Reordering of an existing pattern's notes.
Two-octave progressions whose pitch content together exhausts the chromatic aggregate.
Disjunct scales concatenated (e.g., C major + C# major + D major + Eb major).
Scales in different tonalities played simultaneously.
Simultaneous progressions in different keys AND different rhythms.
Progressions converging toward a central tone.
Rows composed of all 7 different diatonic tones.
Melodic figures using all 12 different tones.

named_chord_constructs._description: Specific chord constructs Slonimsky names. Some are his own coinages; some are attributed to other theorists (Klein, Cowell, Scriabin).

constructs.definition: Dominant-seventh with fifth omitted; chromatically tabulated in 12 keys.
12-tone chord, intervals symmetrically invertible around the tritone axis; odd-indexed intervals form a decreasing arithmetic sequence, even-indexed an increasing one.
Series of diminishing intervals from octave to semitone.
12 different notes arranged in thirds, forming 4 mutually exclusive triads.
Two major triads, usually at tritone distance.
Two minor triads, usually at tritone distance.
Chords composed of intervals of whole tones each.
Complex of adjacent notes filling one or more octaves.
6-tone scale C-D-E-F#-A-Bb used by Scriabin in Prometheus.

harmonization_methods._description: Methods Slonimsky catalogs for harmonizing a given scale or pattern.

methods.definition: Harmonize using only chords derivable from the scale's own pitch content.
methods.example: Scale No. 12 (C, D#, F, F#, A, B, C) harmonized in F major + B major triads.

methods.definition: Cycle Octave → Tertian → Quintan → Octave bass position as melody ascends (reverse on descent); produces parallel major triads across tonalities.
methods.example: Tosca Act II whole-tone bass under parallel majors.

methods.definition: Apply Master Chords (dom7 minus 5th); transposable a tritone with satisfactory results.
Each voice uses all 7 diatonic notes with no vertical duplication.

arpeggiation_systems._description: Specific arpeggiation pattern families with their catalog ranges.

families.definition: Arpeggiation by thirds from heptatonic scales.
Arpeggios cycling 4 mutually exclusive triads (e.g., C major, D minor, F# major, G# minor).
Two overlapping 6-tone rows comprising all 12 different tones.

types.definition: Reads the same backward or forward.
Palindromic canon producing 6-tone chords composed of 2 triads.
types.example: Scale No. 7 canonically developed → C major + F# major bitonal chord.

systems.definition: Major tetrachords with diatonic-step gap. Has 48 functionally different notes.

voice_leading_positions._description: Slonimsky's named soprano-voice positions in four-part triad writing.

positions.definition: Root in both melody and bass.
Root in bass, third in melody.
Root in bass, fifth in melody.

theoretical_lineage_cited.name: Domenico Alaleona
theoretical_lineage_cited.contribution: Early proposal of new scales by equal division of octave.

theoretical_lineage_cited.name: Alois Hába
theoretical_lineage_cited.contribution: Classified equal-interval scales with proposed harmonizations.

theoretical_lineage_cited.name: Joseph Schillinger
theoretical_lineage_cited.contribution: Classified new tonal progressions in Theory of Pitch-Scales chapter.

theoretical_lineage_cited.name: Ferruccio Busoni
theoretical_lineage_cited.work: Entwurf einer neuen Aesthetik der Tonkunst

theoretical_lineage_cited.name: Fritz Klein
theoretical_lineage_cited.contribution: Introduced n-interval technique; coined Mother Chord and Pyramid Chord in Die Maschine (under pseudonym Heautontimorumenus).

theoretical_lineage_cited.name: Rimsky-Korsakov
theoretical_lineage_cited.contribution: Deliberate use of 8-tone scale alternating major/minor seconds (Scale No. 393).

theoretical_lineage_cited.name: Debussy
theoretical_lineage_cited.contribution: First deliberate use of whole-tone scale as a device; Voiles combines whole-tone with pentatonic.

theoretical_lineage_cited.name: Schoenberg
theoretical_lineage_cited.contribution: 12-tone technique, treated by Slonimsky as a permutation case of the semitone progression.

theoretical_lineage_cited.name: Scriabin
theoretical_lineage_cited.contribution: Prometheus scale (C-D-E-F#-A-Bb) used in his symphonic poem.

applications_to_jazz_lineage._description: How the Thesaurus connects to the jazz masters distilled elsewhere in this corpus. For the eventual melodic engine: these are the rule_id prefixes downstream consumers will key off when classifying patterns by playing tradition.

connections.thesaurus_application: Equal Division of Octave into Three Parts (Ditone Progression) is the Giant Steps cycle. Multiple Coltrane practice routines documented as Thesaurus-derived.
Linear concept uses Slonimsky-style equal-division pivots extensively; diminished and augmented symmetric divisions central to his vocabulary.
Symmetric-diminished scales and polation patterns visible across his Mahavishnu Orchestra and acoustic output.
Wide-interval polations and chromatic infra-inter-ultrapolation shape his improvisational vocabulary.

applications_to_jazz_lineage._distillation_note: These connections are MAINTAINER-attested per session memory + general jazz scholarship. Codifying them as engine rules requires a separate Phase 7 pass that maps Coltrane/Martino/McLaughlin documented practice routines onto specific Thesaurus patterns. v0.1 systems-draft establishes the taxonomy only; the player-to-pattern bindings come in v0.2.

v01_distillation_completeness.next_phase: Pattern catalog distillation requires notation-OCR (Audiveris) or manual transcription. v0.1 melodic_rules can fire on TAXONOMY (polation operation + equal-division family + progression category) without specific pattern bindings. v0.2 adds the 1500+ pattern catalog.
